name: navigator-agent-builder-surface-coherence
body:
The distributed `codebase-navigator` prompt `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` must accurately account for the `agent-builder`'s main-write surface WITHOUT restating it: it REFERENCES the agent-builder's own definition (`opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`) as the authoritative enumeration of that surface, and states only what the NAVIGATOR needs operationally.

Why: the prompt today under-describes the surface in three places — it names only `.opencode/agents/**`, when the agent-builder also maintains the repo-root `AGENTS.md` (hygiene, `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-agents-md-hygiene`) and the `opencode.json` agent→model map (`requirements.requirement.agent-builder-model-map`) on the main checkout, all THREE under the SAME carve-out 1 of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`. The stale spots are: the project-flow carve-outs paragraph (lines 176-181, names only `.opencode/agents/**` as the one committed work surface), the ""Codebase agents"" bullet (lines 508-512, ""its only write grant is `.opencode/agents/**`""), and the scoped ""Main is never a mutation place"" bullet (lines 524-529, names only the `.opencode/agents/**` edits).

Required behaviour:
- REFERENCE, DO NOT RESTATE: the navigator prompt points at the agent-builder's own definition for the surface enumeration instead of carrying a subset that can go stale. (Symmetry: `requirements.constraint.agent-builder-agents-md-hygiene`'s process-ownership rule makes the navigator the sole owner of the canonical change-set process; likewise the agent-builder owns the enumeration of its own write surface.)
- NAVIGATOR-OPERATIONAL: it still states what the navigator must do — when code-writer agents are missing or outdated it tasks the `agent-builder` on the MAIN checkout, the agent-builder commits there, then the navigator rebases the project worktree onto main, re-scans the worktree, and the user restarts opencode and reconnects before implementation continues.
- SURFACE COVERAGE: that delegation is stated to include the repo-root `AGENTS.md` hygiene and the `opencode.json` agent→model map ALONGSIDE the `.opencode/agents/**` scaffold, so the navigator knows the maintenance spans all three carve-out-1 paths.
- SCOPING: the ""Main is never a mutation place"" scoping names all three carve-out-1 paths (not only `.opencode/agents/**`), retains the optional consented `release-agent` as the other agent carve-out, and keeps the two-carve-out count unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- No spot in `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` says or implies the agent-builder's write grant/surface is ONLY `.opencode/agents/**`.
- The prompt references the agent-builder's own definition for the full surface, and states the delegation covers the `.opencode/agents/**` scaffold, the `opencode.json` model map, and the repo-root `AGENTS.md` hygiene.
- The on-main → commit → rebase-worktree → re-scan → user-restart-opencode flow is stated, and ""never mutate main"" scopes to the binary's node/edge/plan/review mutations, not to the delegation.
- Scope is the one product-source file `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are NOT edited by this requirement.
